families.name: Landing on a sparse target
families.question: Does the orbit of an expanding piecewise-affine map ever land exactly on a sparse set, with about one target per doubling of scale (numbers like 5·2^k − k − 6)?
families.heuristic: At scale N an orbit point hits a target with chance about c/N. The orbit grows geometrically, so the chances form a convergent geometric series dominated by its first unchecked term.

families.name: Euclid's algorithm with multiplication
families.question: Two counts play a subtractive Euclid game in which the smaller count is also multiplied (by 2 or 3) each round. Do the two counts ever come out equal, or off by one exact small constant?
families.heuristic: The ratio of the two counts moves like a chaotic orbit of an expanding interval map, so the difference is about as large as the counts. Hitting one exact value has chance about 1/size per round, and the sizes grow geometrically.

families.name: Powers of two in a 2-adic valuation sequence
families.question: Write D = 2^v (2a + 1). The sequence D -> D + a + v + c (Katelyn Doucette's form) or a base-3 analogue. Does it ever reach a power of two (or of three)?
families.heuristic: If the low digits of the terms are random, an n-bit term is a power of two with chance about 2^-n. The terms grow geometrically, so the total chance after the computed terms is negligible.

families.name: Antihydra-type walk with drift
families.question: A number is multiplied by about 3/2 or 4/3 each round, and a counter goes up or down by its last digit (parity, or residue mod 3). The counter drifts upward. Does it ever reach zero?
families.heuristic: If the digits behave like fair coins or dice, the counter is a random walk with positive drift. From height h it ever returns to zero with chance ρ^h (gambler's ruin), and h is already in the thousands to hundreds of thousands.

families.name: Nested counters and stacks
families.question: A fast 3/2 counter drives a stack of slower counters, or a small counter must catch up with a large one. Does the whole stack ever empty, or the small counter ever reach the threshold?
families.heuristic: The depth that the fast counter reaches into the stack falls off geometrically while the stack grows. Emptying it needs a run of coincidences, each about as unlikely as a Collatz hit.

families.name: Digit recursion in base 6
families.question: A number is peeled digit by digit in base 6. Does the recursion ever end exactly on a repunit-type value (a block of trailing base-6 digits that runs off the end)?
families.heuristic: For a block of D base-6 digits the halting pattern has chance about 6^-D, and D grows by a constant per round.

families.name: Decision at the end of an exponentially long epoch (probably halts)
families.question: A 3/2 or 4/3 iteration runs for a precisely determined, exponentially long epoch. At its end one parity or residue decides between halting and a new, vastly longer epoch. Which residue comes up?
families.heuristic: Each epoch end halts with a fixed chance p (1/5 to 3/4). So the machine halts with probability 1, but the next undecided epoch is far beyond any computation: deciding it needs one specific bit of an iterate with billions of digits or more.

collatz.name: The Collatz (3x + 1) problem
collatz.text: Every orbit of a map like n -> n/2, 3n + 1 is conjectured to reach 1. This is open (Lagarias's surveys collect what is known). All of these machines ask the same kind of question about one specific orbit of a similar map.

tao.name: Tao (2019): almost all Collatz orbits attain almost bounded values
tao.text: The strongest known positive result is about almost all starting values, in logarithmic density. It says nothing about one specific orbit, and one specific orbit is what each machine asks about.

conway.name: Conway (1972); Kurtz and Simon (2007): generalized Collatz maps are undecidable
conway.text: Maps n -> a_i n + b_i, chosen by n mod m, can simulate any Turing machine. So whether such an orbit reaches a set is undecidable in general (Kurtz and Simon showed the universal form is Π⁰₂-complete). No uniform method exists, and each machine needs an argument of its own.

mahler.name: Mahler's 3/2 problem (Z-numbers, 1968)
mahler.text: Is there a real ξ > 0 with frac(ξ(3/2)^n) < 1/2 for every n? This is open. Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington (1995) proved that the fractional parts of ξ(p/q)^n spread over an interval of length at least 1/p. The parities of the iterates of x -> ⌊3x/2⌋ are exactly such fractional-part events (Akiyama, Frougny and Sakarovitch, rational base 3/2 numeration, 2008). Controlling them along one orbit is beyond known methods.

antihydra.name: Antihydra (bbchallenge cryptid)
antihydra.text: 1RB1RA_0LC1LE_1LD1LC_1LA0LB_1LF1RE_---0RA. It halts iff the walk x -> ⌊3x/2⌋, with a counter +2 on even and −1 on odd, ever goes below zero. The bbchallenge community treats it as the standard example of a Collatz-like cryptid. Its halting status is open, and a proof either way would be a result about the parity sequence of ⌊3x/2⌋.

hydra.name: Hydra (bbchallenge cryptid)
hydra.text: Hydra is a cryptid of the same 3/2 kind as Antihydra. In it the counter must hit zero at the end of a long countdown. The 'probably halts' machines here share its shape: the outcome is a fair coin at the end of an exponentially long run.

spaceneedle.name: Space Needle and Doucette's sequences
spaceneedle.text: 1RB1LA_1LC0RE_1LF1LD_0RB0LA_1RC1RE_---0LD (Space Needle) halts iff D -> D + v + 3a (D = 2^v (2a+1)) from 6 ever reaches a power of two. Katelyn Doucette wrote the reduction in this form. The community has checked 10^8 terms. The other four machines here share the form with other constants.

erdos3.name: Erdős's ternary digits of 2^n (1979)
erdos3.text: Erdős conjectured that 2^n has a digit 2 in base 3 for every n > 8. It is open, and it is the classic example of a question about the digits of an exponentially growing orbit in another base. The base-6 recursion and the power-of-two targets are questions of this type.

gambler.name: Gambler's ruin (the heuristic model)
gambler.text: A random walk with steps +s_i and positive drift returns from height h with probability ρ^h, where ρ < 1 solves E[ρ^step] = 1. This is the source of the heuristic numbers on this page. It is a model, not a theorem about any machine.

residue.name: No residue obstruction
residue.text: For the subtract-and-multiply maps, the residues reachable modulo every 2^a 3^b up to 7,776 include the halting class (tools/number-theory/residues.py). So no congruence alone can prove non-halting; a proof must control sizes, not only residues.

machines.state: runs of 1s [r0, r1, ..., rk] at each visit of the left end
machines.map: r0 += 2; the first odd run r_j is joined with the next one (W = r_j + r_(j+1) + 2), and an even-run cascade runs left. Level by level, an epoch counter follows m' = 3m/2 + d (d ∈ {−2, +1, +4} for even m, {−1/2, +5/2} for odd m), and its parities drive a stack of slower counters.
machines.halt: a visit at which every run is even (so the whole stack must be used up)
machines.lean: lean/Visit.lean halts_iff: HaltsFromBlank ↔ ∃ n, orbit n = none
machines.heuristic: The depth reached into the stack falls off geometrically while the stack grows linearly, so emptying it is very unlikely. An adversarial search over parities found no halting class among 5,000 contexts. The number of even runs is always odd, but that does not rule out a halt.
machines.gap: none in the reduction; an invariant on run parities would settle it (tier B)

machines.map: b odd: a -> about 3a/2 (by a mod 4) and b moves by −5, 0, +8 or +3. Both even: the smaller is subtracted from the larger and a is tripled, swapping when b was smaller (16 rows per letter).
machines.halt: b = 1 with a ≡ 0 (mod 4)
machines.lean: lean/Map.lean next_sound (the map for every even a, the only kind the run meets); lean/Orbit.lean not_halts_of_orbit (if the orbit never gets stuck, no halt)
machines.heuristic: From random starts at scale S, the halting frequency is about 2/S. After 10^6 passes, the chance of a later halt is about 10^-96,600.
machines.gap: the converse direction (a stuck orbit halts) is not stated; the odd-a rows are checked by simulation only, and the run never uses them

machines.lean: lean/Iff.lean halts_iff; lean/Closed.lean pstep_closed, pstep_halt (closed form for every n)
machines.heuristic: Chance about 2^-k per round at level k. After 10^5 rounds (k ≈ 66,605) a later halt has chance about 10^-20,000.
machines.evidence: 2,000 rounds in Lean (about 10^798 steps), 10^5 in Python
machines.gap: none; same function as ranks 5 and 6 from another start

machines.state: X(K, m) = D> (10)^K 1^m; round starts D> 10 1^N
machines.map: N' = 3N + 24 + 6j − 20·2^j (j doublings). In n with N = 2n + 2 this is the same f(n) = 3n − 10·2^k + 3k + 14.
machines.halt: a remainder m = 0, i.e. N = 10·2^j − 2j − 10, i.e. n = h_k
machines.heuristic: Chance about 1/(5·2^j) per round. After 10^6 rounds a later halt has chance below 10^-200,000; the closest approach was 3.8·10^-6 of the range.

machines.map: next(n) = 3n − 2c_i + i + 3 for c_i < n < c_(i+1), c_i = 10·2^i − i − 7; the same f with h_k = c_(k−1)
machines.halt: n = c_(i+1) exactly
machines.heuristic: Chance about 1/(10·2^i) per step at level i. After 8·10^6 map steps the expected number of later hits is about 2^-800,000.

machines.state: two blocks (10)^x 1^y; phases E(x, z), R(x, y), Q(m, k, t)
machines.map: left phase E(x, z) -> E(2x+4, z−2x−6); right phase R(x, y) -> R(x−(y+3)/2, 2y+5); the blocks double at each other's expense
machines.halt: an all-ones tape 1^n with n = 0 or n = 20·2^k − 2k − 12 (8, 26, 64, 142, ...)
machines.lean: lean/Phases.lean halts_iff (the phase map); lean/Fatal.lean ones_fatal_all, ones_safe_all (the fatal lengths, for every n)
machines.heuristic: All-ones tapes are rare: the tape width grows like t^(1/3), and the all-ones lengths grow by a factor of a few each time. A length near n is fatal with chance about 1/n, so a later halt has chance of order 10^-10.
machines.evidence: 10^11 phases (about 4·10^30 steps); all-ones lengths 2, 28, 492, ..., 58,442,346,273, none fatal
machines.gap: that a halt needs an all-ones tape is checked by probing small tapes, not stated in Lean

machines.state: two blocks (10)^x 1^y, as rank 7
machines.map: the same doubling phases as rank 7, with other constants
machines.halt: an all-ones tape 1^n with n ∈ {0, 6} or n = 32·2^k − 2k − 12 (20, 50, 112, ...)
machines.lean: lean/Phases.lean halts_iff; lean/Fatal.lean (fatal lengths for every n)
machines.heuristic: As rank 7: a later halt has chance of order 10^-10.
machines.evidence: 10^11 phases; 30 all-ones tapes, the last of length 15,210,719,738, none fatal
machines.gap: as rank 7. It follows rank 9 for long stretches; the two part only at all-ones tapes and never agree there (holdouts/EQUIVALENCES.md)

machines.state: two blocks (10)^x 1^y, as rank 7
machines.map: the same doubling phases as rank 7, with other constants
machines.halt: an all-ones tape 1^n with n = 3 or n = 28·2^k − 2k − 13 (15, 41, 95, 205, ...)
machines.lean: lean/Phases.lean halts_iff; lean/Fatal.lean (fatal lengths for every n)
machines.heuristic: As rank 7: a later halt has chance of order 10^-10.
machines.evidence: 10^11 phases; 23 all-ones tapes, the last of length 9,908,670,666, none fatal

machines.state: two blocks (10)^x 1^y, as rank 7
machines.map: the same doubling phases as rank 7, with other constants
machines.halt: an all-ones tape 1^n with n = 1 or n = 12·2^k − 2k − 9 (3, 13, 35, 81, ...)
machines.lean: lean/Phases.lean halts_iff; lean/Fatal.lean (fatal lengths for every n)
machines.heuristic: As rank 7: a later halt has chance of order 10^-10.
machines.evidence: 10^11 phases; 30 all-ones tapes, the last of length 14,325,742,934, none fatal

machines.state: pass starts PS(a, c) = B> 0 0 (10)^a 1^c
machines.map: plain pass (a, b) -> (2a + 2, b − 2a − 2); a rebound off the right end gives (2a − b − 1, 3b + 4 − 2a). Doubling and folding of a inside a width that grows by about 2 per pass.
machines.halt: a pass start PS(a, c) with c ≤ 1 (b = 0 at the end of a pass)
machines.heuristic: Only passes with even b can halt, and they come in short chains of doublings that need b = 2a + 2 exactly. That has chance about 1/width per even pass. Even passes are rare (166 in 10^8), so the expected number of later hits is small, but it decays only slowly.
machines.gap: no closed form for the pass map

machines.map: six cases: B (x+1, m, s) -> (x, m+4, 1−s); R (0, m) -> ((m+6)/2, 1 + 2s, 0); C doubles m along a chain, m -> (m+7)·2^i − 7; A and A' double x
machines.halt: a chain of C steps from (x, m, 0) with x = (m+7)(2^(k+1) − 1)/2 − k − 1; after an R step with m = 1 that is x = 2^(k+3) − k − 5 (3, 10, 25, 56, 119, ...)
machines.lean: lean/MapThm.lean halts_iff; lean/Chain.lean halts_iff_chain: HaltsFromBlank ↔ ∃ t x m k, orbit t = some (x, m, false) ∧ m odd ∧ x + k + 1 = (m + 7)(2^(k+1) − 1)/2 (crit_m1: after m = 1 this is x = 2^(k+3) − k − 5)
machines.heuristic: The sum of 1/h over doubling chains is 0.3187 over the whole orbit, and under 10^-4 after round 20.
machines.evidence: 10,000 R steps (29 million C steps) in Python
machines.gap: which steps can start a chain is not stated in Lean (halts_iff_chain_start only excludes a C step just before)

machines.state: E-events E> 0^6 (10)^n T with tail T ∈ {1, X_k, Y_k, Z_k}
machines.map: tail 1: n -> 3n/2 (+ constants); tails X_k, Y_k: n -> (9n + c)/8 by n mod 8, and the small counter k moves by −2..+1 or is multiplied by 3/2 at one pass in 8
machines.halt: only from a Z_k event with n < 12k + 12, i.e. the small counter k must catch up with n/12
machines.lean: lean/Map.lean next_sound (every tail, outside Z_k with n < 12k + 12); lean/Orbit.lean not_halts_of_orbit, no_halt_100k
machines.heuristic: k is reset every phase and grows only occasionally, while n grows every pass. The chance of some phase reaching k ≈ n/12 is about (n/12)^-1.2. After pass 70 the margin n/(12k+12) is above 10^6.
machines.evidence: 10^5 passes in Lean (native_decide), n with 8,063 digits
machines.gap: the region Z_k with n < 12k + 12, where a halt could come from, is not mapped (the orbit never enters it)

machines.state: solid blocks Z(t) = 1^t A>
machines.map: F(t) = 3t/2 + 1 or 3t/2 + 3 for even t; for odd t a doubling loop (a, d) -> (2a+3, d−a−2) from (1, (t+3)/2) that ends in S(a−1−d, 2d+2), 4a + 4 or a restart
machines.start: Z(0) (the blank tape), then Z(19), Z(44)
machines.lean: lean/Reset.lean halts_iff_H: HaltsFromBlank ↔ ∃ n s, orbitFrom (z 44) n = some s ∧ InH s, with InH (z t) := ∃ s, t + 2s + 11 = 2^(s+3)
machines.heuristic: One halting value per doubling band, and the orbit grows about 1.3 times per reset. Chance about 1/t per reset, a convergent sum.
machines.evidence: 10,000 resets in Lean (native_decide); accelerated run to 3.3·10^1615 steps

machines.state: three counters X(a, b, c), Y(a, b, c), Z(a, c)
machines.map: 20 rules: in X the left block gives 3 ones and the middle gains 2 pairs per 1 of the right block; in Y the reverse; a round doubles and then runs a short Euclid-like endgame
machines.halt: Z(a, 2): a Y run whose middle block empties exactly when the right block has 3 ones (c − b = 3)
machines.heuristic: Halting needs c − b = 3 exactly in a Y run, chance about 1/N per round, and N grows about 2.4 times a round. The closest approach after round 3 was about 10^-5.5 N.
machines.gap: no closed form of the round map N -> N'

machines.state: (c, u, v): left block, fast wheel, modulus
machines.map: u -> 2u mod v while v grows by one every operation; c counts the wrap-arounds allowed; at c = 0 a reset sets c = 2(v − u − 1), u = 2u − v, v = u + 3
machines.halt: a reset with 2u = v exactly
machines.lean: lean/Doubling.lean halts_iff_op: HaltsFromBlank ↔ ∃ n, opIter n (0, 2, 5) = none
machines.heuristic: A reset finds 2u − v anywhere in [0, v), so a halt has chance about 1/v per reset, and v grows about 1.47 times per reset. A later halt has chance about 10^-10.

machines.state: round starts B> 0 0 1^a 0 1^b (one or two blocks)
machines.map: even blocks n -> 5n/2 + 1; odd blocks are divided by 6 digit by digit. One block: n = 6^j·m + (6^j − 1)/5 with m ≢ 1 (mod 6) goes to n + 3m/2 + 1 + j (m even), n + 3 + j (m ≡ 3), or two blocks (m = 6q + 5)
machines.halt: m = 0: the block is a base-6 repunit (0, 1, 7, 43, 259, ...), or a nested recursion ends exactly (second block 5, 41, 257, ...)
machines.start: C(0, 2, 0); the rounds E 2, E 6, E 16, E 41, ...
machines.lean: lean/DMMap.lean halts_iff: halts iff the orbit of next from C(0, 2, 0) reaches none (DeepMind's map, proved here in core Lean)
machines.heuristic: For a block of D base-6 digits the halting pattern has chance about 6^-D. After 10^6 rounds D is about 263,000.
machines.evidence: 10^6 rounds of the round map (block with about 205,000 decimal digits)
machines.gap: the per-round digit description is computed; the Lean map is DeepMind's sweep-level form

machines.state: two blocks of ones (a, c), a even
machines.map: c even: (a − c + 12, 3c − 6) if c ≤ a + 8, (c − a − 10, 3a + 27) if c ≥ a + 14; c odd: (a − c − 1, 3c + 6) if c ≤ a − 5, (c − a + 3, 3a) if c > a
machines.halt: c − a ∈ {10, 12} (c even) or a − c ∈ {1, 3} (c odd)
machines.heuristic: c − a is about as large as c. The chance is about Σ 4/c_k, and c grows about 1.236 times a round.

machines.state: W(p, 0, r): p pairs and a reservoir of r ones
machines.halt: r = p + 1
machines.heuristic: The leftover r is spread over about 2p values, so the chance is about 1/(2p) per run of doublings, and p grows exponentially. No modulus below 200 excludes the halting pairs.

machines.state: P(u, v), Q(u, v): pairs of 1s
machines.map: P: u < v -> P(3u + 2, v − u − 1); u ≥ v + 2 -> Q(3v + 3, u − v − 2). Q: u < v -> Q(3u + 3, v − u − 1); u ≥ v + 2 -> P(3v + 5, u − v − 2). The smaller count is subtracted and tripled.
machines.halt: u = v or u = v + 1
machines.lean: lean/Reduction.lean halts_iff' : HaltsFromBlank ↔ ∃ n k u v, orbit n = some (k, u, v) ∧ (u = v ∨ u = v + 1)
machines.heuristic: The direction u/(u+v) follows an expanding map like x -> 3x/(1+x). The chance of landing on the diagonal is about 1/(u+v), and after 10^6 rounds the total is about 2^-300,000. Residues mod 2 to 39 do not exclude the diagonal.

machines.state: R1(i, j), R2(i, j): blocks of 2i and 2j ones, flag J
machines.halt: i = j or i + 1 = j
machines.lean: lean/Round.lean halts_iff: HaltsFromBlank ↔ ∃ n, orb n = none
machines.heuristic: i − j behaves like a random number of the size of i, so the chance is about 2^-n per round with n-bit numbers.

machines.state: left-end states A(n, k), D(n, k) = 1^n (01)^k 111
machines.map: n odd: double n, paying (n+5)/2 pairs, D(2n + 7, k − (n+5)/2); if the pairs do not suffice, give the ones back and double the pair block instead; n even: drain, each 01 becomes four 1s
machines.halt: n odd and k = 1 (a doubling in D that leaves exactly one pair, 2k = n + 7)
machines.heuristic: Each doubling stage ends with a remainder spread over about n/2 values, so the chance is about 2/n per stage, about 2^-10,000 now.

machines.state: ones with one hole; samples S(p, r)
machines.map: hole at odd p jumps to (p − 3)/2, else the tape grows by p/2 + 2. In Doucette's form, D = p + 3 = 2^v (2a + 1) goes to D + a + v + 1
machines.halt: D reaches a power of two (a run of halvings ends at p = 1, a tape length 2^j − 1)
machines.lean: lean/Doucette.lean halts_iff_doucette; lean/Map.lean halts_iff; lean/Bound.lean no_halt_10_3669
machines.heuristic: An n-bit term is a power of two with chance about 2^-n. After 30,000 terms (1,835 digits) the chance is negligible.

machines.state: one block of n ones
machines.map: with D = n + 2 = 2^v (2a + 1): D -> D + a + v + 2 (D = 3·2^v with v even and positive is an exception)
machines.halt: D reaches a power of two
machines.heuristic: Only about 1.3 values per binary length end the run, and the orbit spends about 2.5 passes per length. From 80,223 bits on, the chance is about 2^-80,000.

machines.state: two blocks K(p, q)
machines.map: odd p is halved to (p − 3)/2, even p becomes 3p/2 + q. In Doucette's form, D = p + 3 = 2^v (2a + 1) goes to D + a + v
machines.halt: D reaches a power of two (with q = 1)
machines.lean: lean/Doucette.lean halts_iff_doucette; lean/LowerBound.lean (no halt before 2^2073 steps)
machines.heuristic: Near X, p is 3 below a power of two with chance about 1/X, and p grows geometrically. After 200,000 iterations (40,089 bits) the chance is negligible.

machines.state: ones with one hole; samples S(p, r)
machines.map: base 3: the hole at p ≡ 2 (mod 3) jumps to (p − 2)/3, else the tape grows by about a third. In Doucette's form, D = p + 1 = 3^v (3a + ρ) goes to D + a + v + 2 + ρ
machines.halt: D reaches (3^v, r) with v + r ≡ 1 (mod 3); not every power of 3 halts
machines.heuristic: An n-digit term in base 3 is a power of 3 with chance about 3^-n, and only one residue of v in three halts. After 30,000 terms (1,874 digits) the chance is negligible.

machines.state: Space Needle: block lengths at the left end
machines.halt: D reaches a power of two
machines.heuristic: If the low bits are random, v is geometric with mean 1 and D grows about 1.92 times per term (0.941 bits). An n-bit term is a power of two with chance 2^-n.
machines.evidence: 3·10^6 terms here (2.8·10^6 bits); the community reports 10^8

machines.map: n even: n -> 3n/2 + 2, m -> m + 2; n odd: n -> (3n + 7)/2, m -> m − 1. With a = n + 4 this is Antihydra's a -> 3a/2 / 3(a+1)/2
machines.halt: an odd n meets m = −1
machines.heuristic: With fair-coin parities the counter is a walk with steps +2 and −1 (drift +1/2). It returns from m with chance φ^-(m+2), φ = 1.618. From 50,008 that is about 10^-10,450.
With fair residues k is a walk with steps +1 (chance 2/3) and −1 (1/3). It returns from k with chance 2^-k, and k = 331,763 after 10^6 rounds.

machines.state: walls (z, y): a wall of 0s and a block of 10s
machines.halt: the orbit leaves the rules only at y = 0 with z not a multiple of 3; from some of those walls the machine halts (C 92 0 does, after 54,805 steps), from others it does not
machines.lean: lean/Reduce.lean not_halts_of_orbit (if the orbit never reaches y = 0 with 3 ∤ z, no halt). DeepMind's full halts-iff (cryptids, Mathlib) is stated as an axiom in lean/DeepMindMap.lean and not used.
machines.heuristic: With fair residues y is a walk with steps +4, +6, −1 (drift +3). It reaches 0 from height y with chance ρ^y, ρ = 0.3349. After the first step y was never below 4.
machines.evidence: 10^4 walls in Lean (native_decide, more than 10^2400 steps), 10^6 in Python (y = 2,999,377)
machines.gap: the converse (an exit actually halts) is not proved, and not every exit halts

machines.state: Antihydra: Q(p, a, 2) = 1^p 0 1^a 0 11 B>
machines.map: x -> ⌊3x/2⌋ (x = a + 5); the counter p goes +2 when x is even, −1 when x is odd
machines.halt: the counter would go below 0
machines.heuristic: With fair-coin parities p is a walk with drift +1/2 that returns from p with chance φ^-(p+1). After 10^6 steps p = 498,505.
machines.evidence: 10^6 steps of the walk (x with 584,967 bits)
machines.gap: none; this is the community's reference cryptid

machines.map: a period trades 5 words 10110110 for 31 words 1100: (n, m + 5) -> (n + 31, m). A phase ends at r = m mod 5 < 5 and resets by a table (r = 0: new phase with m' = ⌈(n+4)/2⌉; r = 1, 2: (n + 12, 0), (n + 32, 0); r = 3, 4: new phase with m' = ⌊(n+25)/2⌋, ⌊(n+26)/2⌋), while the tail t loses 1 to 4 words. When the tail runs out it is rebuilt with about 3.1 n words: a second level.
machines.halt: on the second level, some remainder classes at a nearly empty tail halt (for example cfg n 2 with tail 10 (1110)^2 1001101011001), others loop
machines.heuristic: Level 1 ends after about 2,176 more phases (n about 10^770). Whether level 2 halts depends on residues mod 10 of a 770-digit number, so it is a Collatz-like question one level up.
machines.evidence: exact accelerated run to 4.5·10^17 steps; the table iterated to about 10^1541 steps
machines.gap: the reset table is measured, not proved (work in progress)

machines.state: D> 0 0 111 0 1^n T: a block and a short tail word
machines.map: with n = c + 1 + 3t, the next round has n' = 4t + d and a tail T', where (d, T') depends only on (T, c): a 4/3 map with a tail Markov chain
machines.halt: some tails halt
machines.lean: lean/Reduction.lean not_halts_of_orbit (if the round map never halts or gets stuck, no halt), halts_of_orbit (a halting round is a real halt), halts_iff under the hypothesis that the orbit never gets stuck
machines.heuristic: With c uniform, the tail is a recurrent Markov chain, and an excursion hits a halting tail with chance between 10^-18 and 10^-13. So the model halts with probability 1, but only after some 10^13 to 10^18 rounds.
machines.gap: the 'never stuck' hypothesis of halts_iff is checked along the orbit, not proved in general

machines.state: epochs: a run of c ones eaten 4 at a time while a block X grows
machines.map: X -> ⌊3X/2⌋ + 5 per phase; at the end of an epoch c mod 4 and the last parity decide halt or a new, vastly longer epoch
machines.halt: the end of epoch 4 halts if x + u is odd at the end of epoch 3, or if it is even and the last u of epoch 4 is 2
machines.heuristic: Epoch 4 halts with chance 3/4 (fair-coin parities), and eventually with chance 1. Deciding it needs the parity after 1.15·10^14 phases (numbers of about 4·10^13 bits).

machines.state: a number u and a fuel counter
machines.map: u -> 3⌈u/2⌉ while the fuel burns; when the fuel runs out the machine halts or turns its number into new fuel
machines.halt: the fuel runs out on an odd point of the u-sequence
machines.heuristic: For fuel 1 to 20,000, 33.6% of rounds halt. So each round halts with chance about 1/3, and the machine with chance 1. The fourth round needs the parity of u_i for i near 1.5·10^22.

machines.state: S(x, c): countdown phases
machines.map: S(x, c + 2) -> S(⌊3x/2⌋ + 7, c); at the end of a countdown, one residue class of x in four halts, else a new countdown of length about x
machines.halt: one residue class mod 4 at the end of a countdown
machines.heuristic: Each phase from 3 on halts with chance 1/4, so the machine halts with chance 1, after a tower of exponentials of steps.
machines.gap: the residue table is read off the proved map, not stated in Lean

machines.map: a -> 3a/2 + 7 (even) or (3a + 7)/2 (odd), Antihydra's map; the 01 pairs are a budget: an even value costs 3, an odd one 1
machines.halt: when the budget is gone, the next even value halts if it is 2 mod 4 (0 mod 4 refills the budget with half the second block)
machines.heuristic: Each budget end is a fair coin, so the machine halts with chance 1. The fifth budget has 2^1479 pairs.

machines.map: n -> about 8n/3 per phase while the stack m drains by 1 or 2; an empty stack resets to about 2n/3 words
machines.halt: the orbit of (14, 5) reaches (1, n) with n ≡ 1 (mod 3)
machines.lean: lean/Map.lean halts_iff; runs_long (no halt in 10^2899 steps)
machines.heuristic: With fair residues the stack lands on m = 1 with chance 3/5 and then halts with chance 1/3, so each cycle halts with chance 1/5. The third cycle needs about 5·10^2901 phases.

machines.state: (a, K, j) = 1^a 0 0 (10)^K 1^(2j+1) C>: a wall, pairs and a block
machines.map: a wall cell is spent per phase while K grows like K -> 3K/2; when the wall runs out the whole tape becomes a new, much longer wall
machines.halt: an epoch ends with K even
machines.heuristic: With fair-coin parities each epoch end halts with chance 1/2, so the machine halts with chance 1, but after more than 10^(10^39989) steps.

machines.map: a -> (3a + 11)/2 (odd) or 3a/2 + 6 (even), Antihydra's map with other constants; each phase costs two pairs of the budget c
machines.halt: a budget ends at a = 1 with b even
machines.heuristic: Each budget end halts with chance about 1/4, so the machine halts with chance 1. The fifth budget holds a 399,947-bit number of pairs.
